limits: The two constructed cases are artificially injected and do not correspond to a real design seen here.
The 0.05 and 0.95 thresholds are chosen, not optimised; this round only shows they do not false-positive on the clean design.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.

one_of_the_two_new_branches_went_unteste.what_happened: both constructed cases fired DOMINATED_ON_EVAL, not NEAR_DEGENERATE. Zeroing 99 percent of a column makes it dominated by the remaining value, so the dominance rule fires first and the ratio rule is never reached.
one_of_the_two_new_branches_went_unteste.so: the NEAR_DEGENERATE branch (evaluation dispersion below 5 percent of training dispersion) is implemented but not exercised by this round
one_of_the_two_new_branches_went_unteste.what_would_exercise_it: a column that keeps its spread but shrinks in scale, for example a continuous feature multiplied by 0.01 on the evaluation set
one_of_the_two_new_branches_went_unteste.why_I_am_recording_it: reporting the tier as validated would overstate what was tested; one branch of two remains untested

what_did_get_validated.clean_design_passes: no false positive on the R148-style design, which is the property that matters most since a noisy check would be ignored
what_did_get_validated.dead_code_still_flagged: the original tier still fires on the reserved-code case
what_did_get_validated.dominance_rule_works: flags at 0.990 against a training rate of 0.147, and at 0.960 against 0.605
